Subject: Network separation synthesis & evidence request — Dedicated/Private

Hi Ellen and Alex,

Thanks again for the intake call this morning. As requested, I'm pulling together a concise "separation synthesis" that shows how Redwood implements network and control boundaries between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. The doc set I'm attaching is intended to satisfy the SIG/CaIQ questions you flagged and give your SOC 2 reviewer a quick map to relevant evidence.

Immediate asks from your side:
- Confirm the top-level scope: Bluewater will review Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) + Private (VPC with customer control plane).
- Tell me if you prefer a single combined network diagram or 2 side-by-side diagrams (Dedicated vs Private).

What I'm attaching in this round:
1) network-seg-diagram-v2.drawio.pdf — simplified layered topology with control/data plane labels and egress paths.
2) control-matrix-dedicated-private.xlsx — mapping of SIG/CaIQ items to artifacts and responsible teams.
3) redwood-inference-boundary-summary.pdf — 1-pager describing our tenant fencing model and fallback routing.

Key considerations for your reviewers (high level):
- Dedicated uses isolated GPU pools with dedicated subnets and strict egress NAT gateways per tenant group; control-plane traffic is routed over a management VPC with restricted peering.
- Private adds customer-managed VPCs where we deploy inference runtime as customer-owned compute; control plane can be configured to stay in Redwoods' private link or to run in your VPC via our control-plane connector (see diagram).
- KMS boundaries: Data-at-rest keys for Private can be customer-managed (bring-your-own-key). For Dedicated/Hosted we support Redwood-managed KMS with key access policies that prevent cross-tenant usage.

Next steps: once you confirm scope, Kimberly will add the SIG question crosswalk and we'll schedule a 30-min walkthrough with your SOC reviewer. Proposed times: Tue 1/20 10:00–10:30 PT or Wed 1/21 13:00–13:30 PT.

Thanks,

Mina — thanks for the fast turnaround and attachments. Quick clarifying Qs from our security review before we schedule:

1) Egress controls: for Dedicated, are customer egress flows always NATed through a tenant-specific gateway, or do you use shared egress NATs grouped by tenant pools? We need to know whether IP-level separation is guaranteed.
2) Control-plane reachability: for Private with the control-plane connector, can you provide the minimal set of CIDR ranges and ports that need to be allowed from our side?
3) Audit evidence: do you have an existing sample of the flow logs and KMS key policy snippets that map to the items in the control matrix? A redacted example is fine.

If you can answer inline that will help us triage the SIG items. If it's easier we'll take the 30-min walkthrough and capture the answers in real time.

Hi Alex — happy to answer these inline. I've also attached the control-matrix-dedicated-private.xlsx referenced by Mina; the sheet named "EvidenceSamples" contains the redacted artifacts you asked for.

1) Egress controls:
- Dedicated: tenant traffic is NATed; by default we assign a dedicated egress NAT per tenant-pool when a customer purchases reserved capacity. That NAT allocation is IP-level unique to the pool (no shared NAT across unrelated tenants). We do support pooling for smaller reserved tenants on the same commitment, but that is by explicit contract and documented in the "egress assignment" column of the control matrix.

2) Control-plane reachability (Private connector):
- Minimal outbound: TCP 443 to control.redux.redwood-inference.internal (we will provide the specific IP ranges in the next email/drive).
- Ports: 443 for control plane TLS; 22 only for optional jump-hosts if you enable our remote debug (disabled by default).
- We use short-lived mTLS certificates for connector auth; the connector initiates outbound connections so you do not need to open inbound ports on your VPC.

3) Audit evidence:
- In EvidenceSamples there's a sample flow-log CSV (redacted), a KMS key policy snippet (redacted), and a labeled trace from our tracing service showing control-plane vs data-plane flows. These are redactions of the real artifacts we provide during SOC/SIG packages.

Proposed follow-up: we can confirm exact CIDR ranges in an internal doc and then share a short ACL/CIDR list you can paste into your firewall rules. Tue 1/20 10:00 PT works for me.

Cheers,

Kimberly Park
Lead Security Architect, Redwood Inference
